thread:
Jordan (Acme): Hey team — since ~09:10 UTC our embedding calls are flaky. We expect 1536-dim vectors but a bunch of responses are 768 dims and some requests are timing out 5-15s. Also seeing a lot of traffic routed to eu-west-1 even though we set X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2. Billing spiked from retries. request_id: req_0a1b2c3d

liz (Support): Sorry you hit this — sending to infra/sre. Can you paste a minimal curl + a sample response that shows the dim mismatch? Also confirm model name you called.

Jordan (Acme): Sure — example request we used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-..." \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-std-v2","input":["doc1","doc2"], "batch_size":256}'
```
Sample response (truncated):
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001,0.002,...],"metadata":{}}, {"embedding":[0.003,...]}], "model":"embed-lite-v1"}
```
We got an error in our app logs: `dimension_mismatch expected=1536 got=768` on ~30% of calls.

liz (Support): Thanks — that helps. Adding logs to the ticket. @ryan-oncall can you check router capacity + whether explicit region headers are being honored?

ryan-oncall: On it. I can already see many of Jordan's requests were routed to eu-west-1 at 09:08-09:16 UTC. Router debug snippet:
```
[09:09:12] req=req_0a1b2c3d route_decision=fallback_capacity_shortfall -> eu-west-1 pool_id=eu-pool-3
[09:09:12] req=req_0a1b2c3d explicit_region=us-west-2 honored=false reason=pool_exhausted
```
Looks like us-west pool hit burst capacity and fallback allowed a compatible variant in eu to take traffic.

sahil-sre: Also seeing autoscaler spin up workers in eu-west-1 which incur a coldstart ~8-12s. That explains the latency spikes. There's an additional issue: fallback routing allowed "compatible" model variants that differ in embedding size (embed-lite-v1=768 vs embed-std-v2=1536). That's causing the dimension mismatch in the client.

anna-infra: Root cause (initial): routing fallback logic prioritized functional compatibility (does the model accept input?) not output shape. When capacity shortage occurs we mistakenly allowed different-dim variants. Secondarily, the capacity accounting under high batch_size (>=256) incorrectly reported available warm workers, so router thought us-west was exhausted even though new warm instances were pending.

liz (Support): OK — short-term mitigations?

anna-infra: Temporary mitigations we applied: 1) pinned Jordan's API key to us-west-2 pool (non-fallback) — this is live (applied at 09:42 UTC). 2) reduced the router's willingness to use eu fallbacks for embedding routes (canary). 3) advise customer to decrease batch_size to <=128 while we stabilize.

ryan-oncall: I pushed a pin for API key sk-ACME-... to us-west-2 at 09:42. Monitoring CPU/RPS now — telemetry shows requests from Jordan dropping to us-west and dims returning to 1536. Keeping the pin for 3 hours, then we'll roll with a proper patch.

Jordan (Acme): Thanks. After the pin I see 99% 1536 dims but a few residual 768 responses in the logs from 09:40-09:44 (likely in-flight). We also saw heavy cost due to retries — can billing team scope credit?

liz (Support): Filed INC-9234 for billing review and credits. support-bot created ticket INC-9234.

sahil-sre: Long-term fixes we will do: 1) router patch to only fallback to model variants with matching embedding dimensions for embeddings endpoints (PR ready, in canary). 2) fix autoscaler accounting with batch aware warmup counts. 3) add alerting when explicit region header is ignored.

anna-infra: Quick repro steps for infra QA:
1) configure a customer to prefer us-west-2 and set API key pin = none.
2) set batch_size=256 and send sustained traffic at 80% of us-west steady capacity to trigger fallback.
3) verify router chooses eu fallback and that fallback respects model shape — currently fails this check.

Command used in repro:
```bash
ab --concurrency 200 --requests 5000 \ 
  "curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-...' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2' -d '{\"model\":\"embed-std-v2\",\"input\":["x"],\"batch_size\":256}'"
```

liz (Support): ETA on full fix?

anna-infra: Patch merged to canary at 10:05. We'll observe canary for 30m -> promote to stable if no regressions. Expect full rollout by ~13:00 UTC. Postmortem and remediation plan to follow.

ryan-oncall: Monitoring looks good after pin. Will keep incident open until stable rollout.

Jordan (Acme): Appreciate the quick response. Two asks: 1) confirm once all requests are consistently 1536 dims; 2) paste follow-up PM with root cause + billing outcome.

liz (Support): Will follow up in this thread with updates. Marking as P1 and attaching INC-9234. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Incident INC-9234 updated: status=investigating assignees=[anna-infra, sahil-sre, liz]

sahil-sre: FYI we also found a couple customer-side libraries that silently reshape when receiving 768 vectors — recommending verification in client code as defense-in-depth.

Jordan (Acme): Good call, we'll add a dim-validation check client-side. Thanks everyone.

liz (Support): Closing loop soon — will paste the canary/rollout notes and billing outcome here when available.
